chunks: And al-Najashi, may God have mercy on him, said in his Rijal:
'Our sheikh and teacher, may God be pleased with him — his excellence is more renowned than can be described in fiqh, kalam, hadith narration, trustworthiness, and knowledge.'

key_terms.الثِّقَةِ: thiqa — reliability and trustworthiness in hadith transmission
key_terms.الرِّوَايَةِ: riwaya — the narration and transmission of hadiths
key_terms.الْفِقْهِ: fiqh — Islamic jurisprudence and legal reasoning
key_terms.فَضْلُهُ: his excellence, scholarly merit, and virtue

ai.seo_question: What did al-Najashi write about Sheikh al-Mufid's scholarly excellence in his Rijal?
ai.summary: Al-Najashi (d. 450 AH), the preeminent Shia rijal scholar, records in his biographical dictionary a laudatory statement about his own teacher — identified by Shia scholarship as Sheikh al-Mufid (d. 413 AH) — declaring that his mastery across fiqh, kalam, hadith transmission, reliability, and learning surpasses description. The formula 'أَشْهَرُ مِنْ أَنْ يُوصَفَ' ('more renowned than can be described') is a classical Arabic superlative of the highest scholarly praise, indicating that the subject's reputation is so established it renders enumeration redundant.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
